text:
Teuvo Teravainen's name came up this month for something other than his play. Elliotte Friedman reported, via Hockey.com on Nov. 20, that a Rickard Rakell deal that fell through involved a first-round pick and Teravainen. He's still a Blackhawk, back in the city where he won a Stanley Cup in 2015, and the production has been slow: eight points in 21 games, none of his last ten producing a goal.

The shot has nearly vanished. He has 16 shots all season and 1.6 individual expected goals, and Chicago gets under 44% of the five-on-five chances with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement last season, though it noted he plays with some of the weakest linemates in the league and his results ran behind his chances.

Chicago has won three straight games he has played, without much help from him on the scoresheet. At 32, the question isn't about a slump so much as what his role becomes, and whether the trade talk returns. Watch his minutes, down to 13:53 over his last ten.
